topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi
target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Binary
lecture_lines: Binary uses only zeros and ones.
Each position represents a power of two.
Numbers are sums of power of two.
animations: Create a text label '0' in white (#FFFFFF) and '1' in blue (#3498DB).
Animate '0' and '1' appearing on the screen.
Display a 3-bit binary sequence '101' in yellow (#F1C40F).

sections.title: Introduction to Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Towers of Hanoi has three rods.
Move disks following strict size rules.
Goal is moving the full stack.
animations: Create a stack of 3 disks (small, medium, large) in red (#E74C3C).
Animate moving the smallest disk to the middle peg.
Animate moving the medium disk to the destination peg.

sections.title: The Binary Connection: Identifying the Move
lecture_lines: The rightmost one indicates the disk.
First bit moves the smallest disk.
Second bit moves the second disk.
Third bit moves the third disk.
animations: Display the disk number '1' to '3' as binary values.
Highlight the binary '1' matching the current disk move.
Animate a transition arrow between binary steps.
Color code disk labels in green (#2ECC71).
Fade in the complete binary sequence representation.

sections.title: Application: Predicting the Path
lecture_lines: Total moves equals two to power N.
Subtract one for the exact count.
Three disks mean seven total steps.
animations: Show the binary count incrementing from 000 to 111.
Animate the corresponding peg moves for each increment.
Use a path line to trace movement across pegs.
Highlight the current active binary bit in magenta (#E91E63).
Show the final configuration after all moves.

sections.title: Conclusion: Beyond the Puzzle
lecture_lines: It is the hidden algorithmic DNA.
animations: Display the recursive formula summary in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate a final summary table of binary to move.
Fade out all elements gracefully to the background.
